title: Scribonia
imageAlt: Scribonia, a pale moth-like thri-kreen scholar with four arms, patterned wings, writing tools, and a tall staff
imageCaption: Scribonia — Magi, scholar, teacher, and seeker of dangerous knowledge.
dek: Scribonia refuses to be reduced by anyone else’s category. His reason gives him courage before gods and tyrants—and makes it very hard for him to stop prosecuting an argument.

body:
Scribonia is a collector of useful knowledge. Where Wren asks how a culture knows its stories are true, he returns from its libraries with literacy rates, years of study, Papirak, Wish, and the metaphysics of truth. He thinks mastery is protective and that a sound argument remains unfinished until it is answered.

“I am Scribonia”

When Aria tries to diminish him as a common moth, Scribonia refuses the premise. Moth, Magi, thri-kreen—other people may use any category they like. His identity does not depend on their permission. That self-possession lets him step toward a physically overwhelming opponent and challenge the hatred beneath Aria’s logic.

Knowledge as freedom and leverage

Scribonia understands that ignorance creates dependence. His Delerium research, teaching, and willingness to confront powers such as Aria all grow from the conviction that understanding can create freedom. The danger is symmetrical: mastery can also become leverage over people who do not possess it.

Aria makes that danger physical by trapping Scribonia in a gemstone in July 2025. Scholarship does not protect him from becoming an object inside somebody else’s strategy.

Eugene and a boundary he keeps

When Eugene receives a Delerium-channeling weapon, Scribonia feels envy. He has been entrusted with something Scribonia worked and suffered to understand. Scribonia does not convert that feeling into entitlement.

I am not your teacher anymore, you do not owe me an explanation in every aspect of your life.Scribonia

Scribonia still wants knowledge and control. Here he recognizes a limit to his authority as a mentor: his student’s life remains their own.

Knowledge that outlives one scholar

Scribonia teaches students as well as gathering knowledge for himself. His teaching carries responsibilities beyond the lesson: it can protect people, give them dangerous capabilities, or pass on his own assumptions after he leaves the room.

The capacity to yield

He recognizes that Gartina has more wisdom for a frightened newcomer and initially waits. Minutes later, he is issuing commands and moral judgments again. Recognizing that someone else is better suited to lead does not make it easy for him to keep yielding the conversation.

The last word

Even after being ordered to stop arguing with Aria, he insists on a final declaration that the issue is not dead. His reasoning makes him difficult to intimidate. It also leaves him treating a conversation as unfinished until his own position has been fully heard, even when others have asked him to stop.

Luminar Spires · order confronted by chaos

The Spires attack the premise on which Scribonia’s power depends: predictable relationships between knowledge, intention, and effect. He identifies the field as primal and unstable, cannot guarantee even a cantrip’s result, and chooses to stop before his own mastery becomes a danger to the group.

Meaningless chaos. Pure entropy solidified. I cannot work with this!Scribonia

The restraint matters beside his response to Magnus. Faced with another uncontrolled threat, Scribonia proposes one of the most structured sequences available: locate Magnus, Gate to him, use Feeblemind, contain him, and eventually apply Imprisonment. He does not want Magnus killed because death would return him to Death. This remains a plan, not a completed capture.

Papirak’s surviving work

Scribonia reports that Magnus killed Papirak seeking Wish-unbound knowledge and clarifies that the information was locked away rather than erased. He has begun researching how the Training Dungeon might function without Papirak. He may help keep his dead teacher’s institution operating, although the record does not establish him as Papirak’s successor.

The incomplete chronology

Scribonia’s earliest appearances, Academy history, full Delerium sequence, imprisonment and release, students, and later 2026 scenes remain incomplete. The surviving passages leave gaps between these episodes; the missing transitions and their dates remain unresolved.

Trust, the caverns, and the storm

Before returning to Babel’s caverns, Scribonia admits that earlier terrible ends have left him more afraid of mortality. Olokun offers reassurance; Scribonia resolves to rely more on his companions. In the dark passages he becomes the group’s eyes, sharing what he sees while Gartina supports their quiet approach. Their expedition reaches living captives, and its aftermath brings the survivors’ knowledge into the refuge.

Later he plans paired weather systems for the mountain offensive with Eugene. He wants a decisive strike, but afterward wonders whether the destruction has gone too far. His private appeal to Saturnia receives no answer established by this scene. The visible mountain damage does not settle the fate of Abyss or the island.

30 September · the promise to stay

At Papirak’s funeral, Scribonia says he should have been there to protect the teacher. He commits to leaving a portion of himself in Pristinia to restore the Training Dungeon and to guard, teach and offer aid. The grief and commitment are witnessed. A completed restoration or permanent success of that watch is not yet shown. Read the funeral and its inheritance.

Scene sources: 1.

March 2024 · two ways of taking notes

Scribonia seeks Jako’s experience with natural environments before exploring the ruins. Jako agrees that traveling together offers mutual protection. Along the way, Scribonia catalogs plants and animals and gathers samples; Jako records them in drawings. They exchange explanations of words and childhood customs. Patient observation and teaching accompany the expedition’s combat and search for treasure.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

September 2026 · old notes guide a new expedition

Minerva briefs later explorers to move quietly, watch for aberrations and avoid entering or casting inside the haze. She explicitly cites Scribonia’s notes for the warning that it feeds on spells. She asks the group to report historically interesting finds to her. The briefing establishes inherited precautions and an ongoing research interest; it does not resolve the ruins’ origins or independently prove every hazard rule she repeats.

Scene evidence: 1.

March 2024 · classifying an unfamiliar place

In his location log posted on 8 March, Scribonia calls his base the Homestead and judges its infrastructure and civilian training limited. His proposed response is practical: train, build and explore. His “Level of Advancement: 1” belongs to his own evaluative scheme, rather than an objective rank for Pristinia.

He also records information attributed to the Master Librarian: Rahu lies roughly four or five days west, and Kinnich Ahua a similar journey east. These are reported travel estimates from that note, not fixed distances or a replacement for later maps. His wish to investigate Contamination remains an intention at this stage.

October · the rescue and its cost

Scribonia chooses the western mist over another attempt to use the Spires, refusing magic he cannot control. After a jungle ambush, he uses the seashell retained from the earlier reconnaissance to bring the company to the beach. His mental ward lets him walk into the mist without the visions that overtake his companions; later, enhanced sight reveals illusions, but does not tell him where Arjahn has turned.

His first attempt to take Arjahn out through a portal fails when Arjahn resists. Trying to remove Wren also fails. As the others see loved ones in danger and rescuers as monsters, Abyss appears beside him and threatens their lives. Scribonia refuses the offered bargain and turns to Wish. The mist disperses for miles, the companions are released and Abyss withdraws. Ryvyt has already freed Nymera with Dispel Magic; the wider rescue does not erase that separate success.

Saving the company does not leave its relationships unharmed. Furious, Scribonia slaps Wren and orders the group to leave before the clearing ends. She glares at him, angry that he dismisses an experience she could not control. He later confronts Death’s offer without accepting it, but exhaustion overtakes him: he collapses, cannot walk and says he cannot cast. Nymera carries him toward the refuge while Arjahn escorts them. The scene records this cost without establishing permanent incapacity or a universal price for Wish.

Hunting journeys · company, grief and a pause

On the June supply journey Scribonia offers to use Fabricate once materials are gathered and tries to renew acquaintance through conversation. The attempt strains against Arjahn’s concern for silence and against subjects that hurt the people he is asking. He argues that social bonds matter; that claim does not settle when or how another person should be pressed to discuss them.

By early October, he tells Olokun he is weary from fighting and loss after attending Papirak’s funeral. He joins the hunt, then accepts an invitation to the coast. When Olokun splashes him with water, he starts to raise a shield but lowers his hand and allows it. The scene preserves a brief acceptance of companionship without declaring the grief resolved.

Following a trace through an imperfect collection

Scribonia searches the Library of Nuru for Saturnia and Mage’s Ruin. He finds mentions and a surviving quotation, while the narrator says the ancient primary sources are not in that collection. His inquiry can continue without making the library a complete account of her past.

Fenwick’s simulacrum brings food. The two wizards exchange access to spells, and Minerva offers expedition help. Scribonia plans to breach the Ruin’s lead layer only after gathering a party. These preparations do not establish that the Ruin has been entered or restored.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Rest, judgment and a request for answers

Before the mist expedition, Scribonia challenges Ryvyt to justify coming to Babel and threatens to withhold restoration if he falls without proving himself. Saray rejects treating an untested ally as a liability. Ryvyt refuses to make his wish to help depend on Scribonia’s approval. These are disagreements within the company, rather than an established right for Scribonia to decide who belongs.

Afterward, exhausted in the Refuge, he receives Nymera’s water and Olokun’s coffee. He asks for a divine assembly and questions the foundations of the crusade if Death’s account contains truth. The condition matters: he has not independently verified that account. He later credits Ryvyt’s work. His eventual recovery allows a new hunting journey, while the assembly and suggested mist protections remain uncompleted.

Scenes in sequence

These selected scenes preserve what was knowable when people acted. Dates below identify source postings in UTC; they do not supply an in-world calendar. A later appearance does not settle present status.

  1. 2024-03-08 · player testimony

    Classifying a new settlement

    Scribonia records an early assessment and travel estimates attributed to the Master Librarian.

    Known at this stage
    The notes reflect his judgments and the information available to him.
    Consequence
    His method begins with recording distinctions and asking what is still needed.
    Still unresolved
    His development rank and route estimates are not objective geography or an official town classification.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

  2. 2024-10-12 · quest

    Achievement and self-doubt diverge

    During the relic trial Scribonia credits his students while judging his own accomplishments harshly.

    Known at this stage
    This is his distressed self-assessment.
    Consequence
    The scene preserves vulnerability beside later intellectual reputation.
    Still unresolved
    His claim of having accomplished nothing is not the archive’s historical verdict.

    Receipt 1

  3. 2024-11-21 · quest

    Remembering companions before the battle

    Scribonia deliberately takes in the support and relationships around him before facing Wrath.

    Known at this stage
    He cannot know which companions will survive.
    Consequence
    The scene gives the later losses a personal history rather than a casualty tally alone.
    Still unresolved
    His description of the last Vanguard members is a contemporary perception, not an exhaustive roster.

    Receipt 1

  4. 2026-06-23 · quest

    Connection can become an ill-timed demand

    Scribonia tries to fill the gathering journey with personal conversation and argues for its value when Arjahn objects.

    Known at this stage
    Companions are trying both to survive and to live together again.
    Consequence
    The exchange exposes different needs and boundaries.
    Still unresolved
    No narrator establishes that their disagreement caused the dragon’s attack.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7 · Receipt 8

  5. 2026-10-02 · quest

    A shield lowered for a friend

    After naming his weariness, Scribonia joins the hunt and later lets Olokun’s playful splash reach him.

    Known at this stage
    He describes grief and loss rather than a simple need for sleep.
    Consequence
    A small moment of companionship remains possible.
    Still unresolved
    The scene does not establish the end of mourning.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6

  6. 2026-10-19 · quest

    The ward does not make a rescue simple

    Scribonia remains free of the mist’s visions, but Arjahn resists his portal and Wren’s attempted extraction also fails.

    Known at this stage
    His companions cannot reliably recognize him; clearer sight does not reveal a companion who has turned away.
    Consequence
    Protection of his own mind is useful without making him able to control everyone else’s escape.
    Still unresolved
    The ward’s exact spell name and universal protections are not established by this packet.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7 · Receipt 8 · Receipt 9

  7. 2026-10-19 · quest

    A wide clearing, followed by collapse

    Scribonia uses Wish; the mist disperses, companions are released and Abyss withdraws. He later collapses and needs to be carried.

    Known at this stage
    Ryvyt has independently freed Nymera before the Wish; the clearing is not assumed permanent.
    Consequence
    A group rescue carries physical cost and leaves conflict with Wren and Arjahn to address.
    Still unresolved
    The exact wish wording, duration, permanent mist state and universal spell cost remain unestablished.

relationshipMap.title: Scribonia’s relationship web
relationshipMap.intro: Knowledge is never solitary in Scribonia’s history. Select a connection to see where teaching becomes inheritance, curiosity becomes power, and the pursuit of safety risks becoming control.

nodes.title: Eugene
nodes.subtitle: Former student, independent scholar
nodes.relation: Teaching that must release its claim
nodes.history: Scribonia privately recognizes Eugene’s brilliance even when Eugene presents himself as a burden. Their shared history includes dangerous knowledge, spellbook learning, and the habits of teacher and student.
nodes.consequence: The relationship matures when Scribonia accepts that Eugene is no longer his student and does not owe him every explanation. Instruction remains causal without becoming ownership.
nodes.evidence: Mentorship and later autonomy are established; the full early teaching chronology is incomplete.

nodes.title: Aria / Pride
nodes.subtitle: Captor and philosophical enemy
nodes.history: Aria humiliates, coerces, and imprisons Scribonia in a gemstone. Her claim that power can secure freedom becomes intimate evidence of what power does when another person’s will is treated as expendable.
nodes.consequence: Scribonia’s suffering cannot define every relationship Aria had, but it prevents later tenderness around her from erasing the danger she represented to him.
nodes.evidence: Coercion and imprisonment are established; every private motive around them is not.

nodes.title: Magnus Niriin
nodes.subtitle: Containment target
nodes.history: Scribonia reads Death’s hold over Magnus as ownership and concludes that ordinary trust cannot safely contain the risk. He proposes Gate, Feeblemind, and Imprisonment rather than execution.
nodes.consequence: The plan reveals both discipline and danger: he rejects killing Magnus while becoming willing to remove Magnus’s practical agency for the sake of collective safety.
nodes.evidence: The containment proposal is established; it has not been carried out.

nodes.title: Magic Academy
nodes.subtitle: Students and institutional legacy
nodes.history: Scribonia’s academy turns knowledge from a personal defense into an institution. Marius, Aurélia, Saoirse, and future students inherit not only spells but the habits, fears, and ethical boundaries of their teachers.
nodes.consequence: His historical importance can outlast his body. The academy also makes his methods answerable to the people who must live with what its students learn to do.
nodes.evidence: The academy and teaching activity are established; its full curriculum and governance remain open.

nodes.title: Papirak
nodes.subtitle: Lost witness and inherited obligation
nodes.history: Papirak’s death removes a person and an irreplaceable historical witness. At the funeral, Scribonia admits guilt that he did not protect him and promises to attempt restoration of the Training Dungeon.
nodes.consequence: The promise binds mourning to future work. Scribonia can preserve and teach what remains without pretending reconstruction will restore everything Papirak knew.
nodes.evidence: The grief, promise, and funeral are established; complete restoration remains an unproven belief.

nodes.title: Elenia
nodes.subtitle: Peer in world-altering power
nodes.history: Scribonia and Elenia participate in a mountain-scale intervention of storm, earthquake, avalanche, flood, lava, and steam. At the Luminar Spires, their responses to unstable magic diverge: analysis and containment beside curiosity and experiment.
nodes.consequence: Their combined capability makes cooperation effective and morally dangerous. Each becomes evidence that knowing how to alter the world does not settle whether the alteration is permitted.
nodes.evidence: Shared expeditions are established; their complete personal relationship is sparsely recovered.

nodes.title: Jiangshi
nodes.subtitle: Colleague in hidden knowledge
nodes.relation: Different ways of making the concealed legible
nodes.history: Scribonia and Jiangshi are associated with research that makes hidden magical writing visible, including the Truesight examination of Papirak’s grimoire. Jiangshi’s ethic of presence also resists reducing care to explanation alone.
nodes.consequence: The connection joins technical revelation to a reminder that not every truth a person needs is solved by analysis.
nodes.evidence: The shared investigation is established; a broader working partnership remains incomplete.

nodes.title: Olokun
nodes.subtitle: Living memory subject to correction
nodes.history: Olokun carries older history about Papirak, Wish, and divine intervention. Scribonia corrects one exact point: relevant knowledge was locked away and wrapped in madness, not simply erased.
nodes.consequence: The exchange models useful correction. Olo remains a vital carrier of lived history while Scribonia supplies precision where magical mechanics matter.
nodes.evidence: The correction is established; neither person becomes an omniscient source.

nodes.title: Nymera
nodes.subtitle: Help beyond specialization
nodes.history: Nymera misunderstands Scribonia’s proposed magical prison and apologizes. Scribonia and Arjahn refuse the apology and affirm that her practical help remains valuable elsewhere.
nodes.consequence: A small exchange tests whether specialized knowledge will humiliate outsiders or help them find a meaningful place in shared work.
nodes.evidence: The Luminar Spires exchange is established; the later relationship remains open.

insights.label: Strongest bond
insights.note: Teaching matters most when the student is allowed to become independent.

insights.label: Deepest wound
insights.note: Knowledge and personhood were both placed under another’s control.

insights.label: Public legacy
insights.note: Private mastery becomes a system other people will inherit.

insights.label: Central danger
insights.note: Safety can become domination even when execution is rejected.

profile.personality: Scribonia is analytical, candid, and capable of separating care from control. He values knowledge but resists the idea that teaching creates ownership over another person’s choices, and he can admit uncertainty without surrendering the obligation to keep investigating.
profile.achievements: He belongs to the first Calling, helps map Prima’s earliest dangers, explores the sector dungeon, reaches Gael, preserves Voraketh evidence, teaches at Prima’s Magic Academy, and repeatedly turns fragmentary encounters into records other people can use. His identity as an artwright joins making, magic, and memory. Finds a limited trace of Saturnia, exchanges spells with Fenwick and prepares a party for a still-uncompleted Ruin expedition.
profile.relationships: Eugene’s brilliance is something Scribonia recognizes and supports without demanding obedience. Olokun is a frequent moral and intellectual counterpart; Gartina, Elenia, Jiangshi, Vaemyr, and Alyhotep share much of his expedition history; and his later students make his legacy institutional rather than merely personal.
